title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent increase cap
requirement: An owner may not increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including dwellings and units in mobilehome parks, subject to subdivision (a); a new tenancy’s initial rent is set freely, with the cap applying only to later increases.
exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; housing under public rent or price control with lower annual increases; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable homes owned by natural persons with written notice; owner-occupied duplexes.
interaction: Does not authorize local rent increase limits beyond Chapter 2.7 and does not affect local authority to adopt or maintain rent control.

title: California statewide just cause for termination of tenancy
requirement: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy an owner may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice, and only for the at-fault or no-fault causes listed in the section.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including mobilehome tenancies and units in mobilehome parks, after 12 months of continuous lawful occupation by the tenant, or 24 months for one tenant.
exemptions: Transient hotel occupancy; dormitories; housing where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with an owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable homes with required notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
interaction: Yields to a more protective local just cause ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019; a property is not subject to both.
quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
penalty: Noncompliance voids the written termination notice; an owner who materially violates the section is liable for actual damages, attorney’s fees and costs, and up to three times actual damages for willful conduct, and the Attorney General or local city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.

title: Rent increases must be conscionable and comply with rent control
requirement: A rent increase the tenant refuses to pay supports eviction only if it is not unconscionable and complies with all laws and municipal rent control ordinances; the tenant may withhold the difference while court decides.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies subject to the Anti-Eviction Act; the increase must comply with any applicable municipal rent control ordinance.
interaction: A rent increase must comply with municipal rent control ordinances.

the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and 
must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.

title: No rent increase to cover condominium or cooperative conversion costs
requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of units, the landlord may not raise rents to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion.
coverage_conditions: All tenants in a converted building, whether or not they are eligible for protected tenancy as senior citizens or disabled persons.
exemptions: Rents may still be increased to cover the cost of new services or amenities.
quoted_span:

simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the

title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control
requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any municipal rent control or rent leveling ordinance for 30 years after completion of construction of the building.
coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings; rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt from local rent control ordinances.
exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, and rents subsidized by governmental funding, are exempt from municipal rent control ordinances.
quoted_span:

constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

requirement: A tenant evicted so the landlord can correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord at least five days before removal.

tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs  (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-
61.6(a)).

title: Reprisal eviction and lease-change ban
requirement: A landlord may not evict, substantially alter a lease or refuse to renew because a tenant asserted lease or housing-code rights, complained to a government agency, joined a tenant organization, or refused retaliatory lease changes.
coverage_conditions: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).  The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, 
including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
penalty: The tenant may sue the landlord for damages in a civil action.

title: Security deposit return deadline and double-damages remedy
requirement: Within 30 days after a tenancy ends the landlord must return the deposit plus interest less deductions, with an itemized list of deductions; the deadline is 5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation.

exemptions: No deduction may be made from the security deposit of a tenant who remains in possession of the rental premises.

title: New Jersey security deposit cap

coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in New Jersey in which the landlord collects a security deposit; prepaid funds held to secure future rent, including the last month's rent, count toward the cap.
exemptions: A pet security deposit may not be charged if, combined with the regular deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
quoted_span:

yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: FAIR Act ban on coordinator services and algorithmic rent setting
requirement: No rental property owner, agent, representative or subcontractor may exchange consideration for the services of a coordinator performing a coordinating function over residential dwelling units. The act takes effect the first day of the twelfth month after enactment.
coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in New Jersey, meaning any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended for use as a primary residence, excluding medical, long-term care and detention facilities.
exemptions: Coordinating function excludes research or statistical analysis, published rent estimates made available to the public at no cost, listing databases offered on equal terms and government affordability controls; spreadsheets and query-only databases are not algorithmic devices.
interaction: Construed in addition to the New Jersey Antitrust Act, which continues to apply to the same conduct.
penalty: A violation is a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act and does not limit the application of sections 6 through 17 of P.L.1970, c.73; the Attorney General must maintain a website location to receive complaints.
